title: An inclusion of finite simplicial sets is a chain of one-simplex extensions
statement: Let $U\subseteq V$ be a simplicial subset of a simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with $U_n$ and $V_n$ finite and nonempty for all $n\geq0$, and assume that $U$ and $V$ have finitely many nondegenerate simplices. Then there is a chain of simplicial subsets $U=W^0\subseteq W^1\subseteq\dots\subseteq W^r=V$ ($r\geq0$) such that for every $0\leq k<r$ there are $n\geq0$ and $x\in W^{k+1}_n$, $x\notin W^k_n$, with (1) $W^{k+1}_i=W^k_i$ for all $i<n$, (2) $W^{k+1}_n=W^k_n\cup\{x\}$, and (3) every $z\in W^{k+1}_j$ with $j>n$ and $z\notin W^k_j$ is degenerate (as a simplex of $W^{k+1}$).

source.place: Lemma 018S (lemma-add-simplices), with the conditions of Lemma 018R (lemma-glue-simplex)

proof.text: Mathlib Subcomplex.le_iff_contains_nonDegenerate implies that if U < V then some simplex of V is absent from U. Choose the least degree n with any missing simplex, using Nat.find, and a missing x in V_n. Minimality gives V_i = U_i for every i < n. The simplex x is nondegenerate: if it were degenerate, Subcomplex.mem_degenerate_iff would give a lower-dimensional ancestor in V, hence in U, forcing x into U by closure under simplicial operators.

source.place: Lemma 018S (lemma-add-simplices), proof, induction parameter and base case, expanded using Definition 0175 (definition-terminology-simplicial-sets)

proof.text: Construct W = U sup Subcomplex.ofSimplex x. This is a subcomplex by the complete lattice API, and U <= W <= V by ofSimplex_le_iff. Thus W_i = U_i for i < n. To prove W_n = U_n union {x}, take a new n-simplex z, expressed as S(f)(x) by mem_ofSimplex_obj_iff. If z is nondegenerate then mono_of_nonDegenerate makes f a monomorphism [n] -> [n], so eq_id_of_mono gives z = x. If z is degenerate, mem_degenerate_iff in W supplies a lower-dimensional ancestor, which lies in U by the preceding lower-degree equality; therefore z lies in U, a contradiction. Conversely x and U_n belong to W_n.

source.place: Lemma 018S (lemma-add-simplices), proof, choice of the lowest-dimensional missing nondegenerate simplex

proof.text: If j > n and z is a new j-simplex in W, then z is in the subcomplex generated by x. If z were nondegenerate in S, mono_of_nonDegenerate would give a monomorphism [j] -> [n], contradicting len_le_of_mono. Thus z is degenerate in S, and Subcomplex.mem_degenerate_iff makes it degenerate in W as required.

source.place: Lemma 018S (lemma-add-simplices), proof, construction of W and the omitted closure/finiteness details; Lemma 018R (lemma-glue-simplex), conditions (1)-(3)

proof.text: For finite V, choose a Fintype structure on V.N and let missing(A) be the finite set of nondegenerate simplices of V whose underlying ambient simplices are absent from A. Use strong induction on missing(U).card. If U = V use the length-zero chain. Otherwise steps 1-3 construct W and its first link. The inclusion U <= W makes missing(W) a subset of missing(U), and the nondegenerate simplex x witnesses that this subset is strict. Finset.card_lt_card therefore permits induction for W <= V. Prepend U with Fin.cons, checking successive indices by Fin.cases. Finally identify each range of a subcomplex inclusion with its degreewise object set to obtain the exact stated range conditions. No degreewise finiteness or nonemptiness assumptions are needed in this construction; their original binders are retained unchanged.

split_report.summary: Stacks 018S inducts on the number of nondegenerate simplices of V outside U. Four steps write the nondegenerate-ancestor argument, choose the least missing dimension, verify that adjoining every degeneracy of one simplex really defines a simplicial subset and preserves the induction hypotheses, and complete the induction. No new nodes are required: the omitted details are finite ordinal factorization and simplicial identities from the cited definition. The refreshed slopmaster2 audit is none; searches by id, blueprint tag and key notions in the read-only WeilConjectures/ and Comparator/ found no exact declaration.

Steps 1-4 give the one-simplex-at-a-time chain cited by the lifting argument.

lean.statement: theorem add_simplices (S : SSet.{u}) (U V : S.Subcomplex) (hUV : U ≤ V) (hU_fin : ∀ (n : ℕ), Finite ((U : SSet).obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n)))) (hV_fin : ∀ (n : ℕ), Finite ((V : SSet).obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n)))) (hU_nonempty : ∀ (n : ℕ), Nonempty ((U : SSet).obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n)))) (hV_nonempty : ∀ (n : ℕ), Nonempty ((V : SSet).obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n)))) [SSet.Finite (U : SSet)] [SSet.Finite (V : SSet)] : ∃ (r : ℕ) (W : Fin (r + 1) → S.Subcomplex), W 0 = U ∧ W ⟨r, Nat.lt_succ_self r⟩ = V ∧ (∀ (k : Fin r), W k.castSucc ≤ W k.succ) ∧ (∀ (k : Fin r), ∃ (n : ℕ) (x : (W k.succ : SSet).obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n))), x.1 ∉ Set.range ((W k.castSucc).ι.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n))) ∧ (∀ (i : ℕ), i < n → Set.range ((W k.succ).ι.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk i))) = Set.range ((W k.castSucc).ι.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk i)))) ∧ Set.range ((W k.succ).ι.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n))) = Set.range ((W k.castSucc).ι.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n))) ∪ {x.1} ∧ (∀ (j : ℕ) (z : (W k.succ : SSet).obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk j))), n < j → z.1 ∉ Set.range ((W k.castSucc).ι.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk j))) → z ∈ SSet.degenerate (W k.succ : SSet) j))
